question: Identify the element with an electronic configuration 2,8,1 from among the following options.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** element with an electronic configuration of 2,8,1 is Sodium (Na)**
 
• Sodium has an atomic number of 11, which corresponds to the electronic configuration **2,8,1**.
 
• This **means that a sodium atom has 11 electrons, with 2 in the first energy level (1s), 8 in the second energy level** (2s), and 1 in the third energy level (3s). 
 
• Sodium is highly reactive because it tends to lose its outermost electron to achieve a stable configuration

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Hydrogen (H)**

 
 
• Atomic Number: 1
 
• Electronic Configuration: **1**
 
• Hydrogen has only one electron, hence its configuration is **2,0** (as it has no additional shells beyond the first one).
 
 
 
• **Chlorine (Cl)**
 
 
• Atomic Number: 17
 
• Electronic Configuration: **2,8,7**
 
• Chlorine has a different outer electron configuration with 7 electrons in its outermost shell.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)**
 
 
• Atomic Number: 12
 
• Electronic Configuration: **2,8,2**
 
• Magnesium has 2 electrons in its third shell, so its configuration is **2,8,2**.
